title: Maximal Linear Structures in Nonlinear S-Boxes
summary: Known nonlinear constructions fall one power of two below the maximal proper linear-structure count; whether that maximum is attainable remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether there exists a nonlinear $n\times n$ S-box with exactly $2^{n-1}$ linear structures. An $n\times n$ S-box with all $2^n$ linear structures would be linear, making $2^{n-1}$ the maximum possible number short of linearity, whereas the available constructions attain only $2^{n-2}$ linear structures.

scope.domain: Linear structures of nonlinear square S-boxes and vectorial Boolean functions.
parameters: n: input and output dimension of the square S-box
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a nonlinear n×n S-box can have exactly two to the n minus one linear structures.

citations.label: DEFAULT: Cipher Level Resistance Against Differential Fault Attack

progress.summary: The source reports S-boxes with at most two to the n minus two linear structures and identifies two to the n minus one as the maximum short of linearity. It explicitly leaves attainability of that maximum open.
citation_labels: Anubhab Baksi et al., DEFAULT: Cipher Level Resistance Against Differential Fault Attack
